source: Find every way to write 15 and 9 as a sum of consecutive nat

items.question: Find every way to write 15 and 9 as a sum of consecutive natural numbers. Can 8 be written this way?
steps: 15 as two numbers: 7 + 8 = 15. As three: 4 + 5 + 6 = 15. As five: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 15.
9 as two numbers: 4 + 5 = 9. As three: 2 + 3 + 4 = 9.
8 as two numbers is impossible, since two consecutive numbers make an odd sum.
8 as three numbers needs a middle number of 8 ÷ 3, which is not whole; four numbers starting at 1 already give 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10, which is too big.
items.answer: 15 can be written in three ways and 9 in two ways; 8 cannot be written as a sum of consecutive natural numbers

videos.answer: 15 can be written in three ways and 9 in two ways; 8 cannot be written as a sum of consecutive natural numbers

steps: All eight results are even: 18, 6, 8, −4, 10, −2, 0 and −12.
The results 0, −2 and −4 appear for every set of four consecutive numbers.
items.answer: Eight expressions, and every result is even

source: Take 3 + 4 − 5 − 6. Switch +4 to −4, then switch −5 to +5 in

items.question: Take 3 + 4 − 5 − 6. Switch +4 to −4, then switch −5 to +5 in the original. How much does the value change each time, and what happens to its parity?
steps: Original: 3 + 4 − 5 − 6 = −4.
Switch +4 to −4: 3 − 4 − 5 − 6 = −12. The change is −4 − (−12) = 8, which is 2 × 4.
Switch −5 to +5 in the original: 3 + 4 + 5 − 6 = 6. The change is 6 − (−4) = 10, which is 2 × 5.
Each change is twice the switched number, so it is even and the parity stays even.
items.answer: The value changes by 8 and then by 10, twice the switched number each time, so the parity never changes

videos.answer: The value changes by 8 and then by 10, twice the switched number each time, so the parity never changes

source: Without computing, which of these are even: 43 + 37, 672 − 3

items.question: Without computing, which of these are even: 43 + 37, 672 − 348, 4 × 347 × 3, 708 − 477, 809 + 214, 119 × 303, 543 − 479, 513³?
steps: 43 + 37 is odd plus odd, so even. 672 − 348 is even minus even, so even.
4 × 347 × 3 has the even factor 4, so even. 543 − 479 is odd minus odd, so even.
708 − 477 is even minus odd and 809 + 214 is odd plus even, so both are odd.
119 × 303 and 513³ are products of odd numbers, so both are odd.
Check two of them: 43 + 37 = 80 and 543 − 479 = 64.
items.answer: Even: 43 + 37, 672 − 348, 4 × 347 × 3 and 543 − 479; the other four are odd

videos.answer: Even: 43 + 37, 672 − 348, 4 × 347 × 3 and 543 − 479; the other four are odd

source: Show that 4m + 2q is always even and try it with m = 4, q =

items.question: Show that 4m + 2q is always even and try it with m = 4, q = −9. Then decide whether x² + 2 is always even by trying x = 6 and x = 3.
steps: 4m + 2q is the same as 2(2m + q), so 2 is a factor for every integer m and q.
With m = 4 and q = −9: 4 × 4 + 2 × (−9) = −2, which is even.
With x = 6: 6² + 2 = 38, which is even.
With x = 3: 3² + 2 = 11, which is odd, so x² + 2 is not always even.
items.answer: 4m + 2q is always even; x² + 2 is even only when x is even

videos.answer: 4m + 2q is always even; x² + 2 is even only when x is even

source: Breaking Even: decide and explain

items.question: Determine and explain which of these expressions always give even numbers: 2a + 2b, 3g + 5h, 4m + 2n, 2u − 4v, 13k − 5k, 6m − 3n, b² + 1, 4k × 3j. Write examples and non-examples, as appropriate, for each. Then write a few algebraic expressions which always give an even number.
steps: 2a + 2b is 2(a + b), 4m + 2n is 2(2m + n), 2u − 4v is 2(u − 2v): all always even.
13k − 5k is 8k and 4k × 3j is 12kj: both always even.
3g + 5h is odd when g is 1 and h is 2, giving 13; it is even when g is 1 and h is 1, giving 8.
6m − 3n is odd when m is 1 and n is 1, giving 3; b² + 1 is odd when b is 2, giving 5.
Expressions that always give even numbers: 2x + 6, 10y − 4z and 6p × q.
items.answer: Always even: 2a + 2b, 4m + 2n, 2u − 4v, 13k − 5k, 4k × 3j. Not always even: 3g + 5h, 6m − 3n, b² + 1

videos.answer: Always even: 2a + 2b, 4m + 2n, 2u − 4v, 13k − 5k, 4k × 3j. Not always even: 3g + 5h, 6m − 3n, b² + 1

source: Sort 4, 12, 18, 22, 36 and 42 into numbers of the form 4p an

items.question: Sort 4, 12, 18, 22, 36 and 42 into numbers of the form 4p and numbers of the form 4p + 2.
steps: 4 = 4 × 1, 12 = 4 × 3 and 36 = 4 × 9: these fill rows of four exactly.
18 = 4 × 4 + 2, 22 = 4 × 5 + 2 and 42 = 4 × 10 + 2: each leaves 2 dots over.
So 4, 12 and 36 are of the form 4p, and 18, 22 and 42 are of the form 4p + 2.

source: Show that 12 + 16 and 22 + 6 are multiples of 4, using the f

items.question: Show that 12 + 16 and 22 + 6 are multiples of 4, using the forms 4p + 4q and (4p + 2) + (4q + 2).
steps: Together the leftovers make 2 + 2 = 4, one more full row: 4 × (5 + 1 + 1) = 28.
Both sums are multiples of 4.
items.answer: 12 + 16 and 22 + 6 both make 28, a multiple of 4

videos.answer: 12 + 16 and 22 + 6 both make 28, a multiple of 4

source: Pairs to Make Fours: the third case

items.question: What happens when we add a multiple of 4 to an even number that is not a multiple of 4? Is it similar to the case of the parity of the sum of an even and an odd number? For 4p and (4q + 2), write the explanation and examples.
steps: 4p + (4q + 2) is 4p + 4q + 2, which is 4(p + q) + 2.
The full rows stack up and 2 dots are always left over, so the sum is never a multiple of 4.
Examples: 4 + 6 = 10, 12 + 18 = 30, 8 + 22 = 30; each leaves a remainder of 2 on division by 4.
It is like even plus odd: the leftover can never be paired away.
items.answer: The sum is 4(p + q) + 2, so it always leaves a remainder of 2 and is never a multiple of 4

videos.answer: The sum is 4(p + q) + 2, so it always leaves a remainder of 2 and is never a multiple of 4

source: Figure it Out (number play, question 3)

items.question: When is the sum of two multiples of 3, a multiple of 6 and when is it not? Explain the different possible cases, and generalise the pattern.
steps: Write the two multiples as 3m and 3n; their sum is 3(m + n).
It is a multiple of 6 when m + n is even, that is when m and n are both even or both odd.
Both odd: 3 + 9 = 12. Both even: 6 + 12 = 18. One of each: 3 + 6 = 9, not a multiple of 6.
This matches the parity rules: odd multiples of 3 behave like odd numbers, even multiples like even numbers.
items.answer: The sum is a multiple of 6 when both are odd multiples of 3 or both are even multiples of 3; one of each gives an odd multiple of 3

videos.answer: The sum is a multiple of 6 when both are odd multiples of 3 or both are even multiples of 3; one of each gives an odd multiple of 3

source: Check that 8 divides 16 + 56 and 80 − 24. Then decide whethe

items.question: Check that 8 divides 16 + 56 and 80 − 24. Then decide whether 8 must divide two numbers that add up to 72.
steps: 72 = 48 + 24, and both are multiples of 8.
But 72 = 50 + 22 too, and neither 50 nor 22 is a multiple of 8.
items.answer: 8 divides the sum and the difference of its multiples, always; two numbers adding to a multiple of 8 are multiples of 8 only sometimes

videos.answer: 8 divides the sum and the difference of its multiples, always; two numbers adding to a multiple of 8 are multiples of 8 only sometimes

source: 36 is divisible by 12. Check that 36 is divisible by every f

items.question: 36 is divisible by 12. Check that 36 is divisible by every factor of 12 and that its multiple 108 is divisible by 12. Then decide whether 42, a multiple of 7, is divisible by 28 and by 14.
steps: 108 = 36 × 3, and 108 = 12 × 9, so the multiple is divisible by 12.
42 = 7 × 6. 42 ÷ 14 = 3, so 14 divides it, because 2 is a factor of 6.
42 = 28 + 14, so 28 leaves a remainder of 14: 4 is not a factor of 6.
items.answer: 36 passes every factor of 12 and 108 is divisible by 12 (always true); 42 is divisible by 14 but not by 28 (sometimes true)

videos.answer: 36 passes every factor of 12 and 108 is divisible by 12 (always true); 42 is divisible by 14 but not by 28 (sometimes true)

source: Decide whether each claim is always, sometimes or never true

items.question: Decide whether each claim is always, sometimes or never true: a number divisible by both 9 and 4 is divisible by 36; a number divisible by both 6 and 4 is divisible by 24.
steps: 9 and 4 share no factor except 1, so the LCM of 9 and 4 is 36.
A number divisible by both must be a multiple of 36: 72 is 9 × 8, 4 × 18 and 36 × 2.
The LCM of 6 and 4 is 12, not 24: 12 is divisible by 6 and by 4 but not by 24.
48 is divisible by 6, 4 and 24, so the claim about 24 holds for some numbers.
items.answer: The claim about 36 is always true; the claim about 24 is sometimes true (12 fails, 48 works)

videos.answer: The claim about 36 is always true; the claim about 24 is sometimes true (12 fails, 48 works)

source: Try 7 + 8 and 9 + 12, then explain with algebra why an odd n

items.question: Try 7 + 8 and 9 + 12, then explain with algebra why an odd number plus an even number is never a multiple of 6.
steps: 7 + 8 = 15 and 9 + 12 = 21: both odd, neither a multiple of 6.
Write the even number as 2n and the odd number as 2m + 1.
Their sum is 2(n + m) + 1, which is one more than an even number, so it is odd.
Every multiple of 6 is 6j, which is 2 × 3j, an even number, so the sum can never equal it.
items.answer: Never true: odd plus even is odd, and every multiple of 6 is even

videos.answer: Never true: odd plus even is odd, and every multiple of 6 is even

items.question: For each statement below, determine whether it is always true, sometimes true, or never true. Explain your answer, with examples and non-examples, and justify your claim using algebra. (i) The sum of two even numbers is a multiple of 3. (ii) If a number is not divisible by 18, then it is also not divisible by 9. (iii) If two numbers are not divisible by 6, then their sum is not divisible by 6. (iv) The sum of a multiple of 6 and a multiple of 9 is a multiple of 3. (v) The sum of a multiple of 6 and a multiple of 3 is a multiple of 9.
steps: (i) 2 + 4 = 6 is a multiple of 3, but 2 + 6 = 8 is not: sometimes true.
(ii) 10 is divisible by neither, but 27 is not divisible by 18 and is divisible by 9: sometimes true.
(iii) 1 + 2 = 3 is not divisible by 6, but 8 + 10 = 18 is: sometimes true.
(iv) 6a + 9b is 3(2a + 3b), so it is always a multiple of 3: always true.
(v) 6a + 3b is 3(2a + b): 6 + 3 = 9 is a multiple of 9, but 6 + 6 = 12 is not: sometimes true.
items.answer: (i) sometimes (ii) sometimes (iii) sometimes (iv) always (v) sometimes

videos.answer: (i) sometimes (ii) sometimes (iii) sometimes (iv) always (v) sometimes

items.question: Deepak claims, "There are some multiples of 11 which, when doubled, are still multiples of 11. But other multiples of 11 don't remain multiples of 11 when doubled." Examine if his conjecture is true; explain your conclusion.
steps: Write any multiple of 11 as 11k.
Doubling gives 2 × 11k, which is 11 × 2k, still a multiple of 11.
For example 33 doubled is 66 and 121 doubled is 242, both multiples of 11.
Every multiple of a number stays a multiple when doubled, so the second part of the claim is false.
items.answer: The conjecture is false: every multiple of 11, doubled, is still a multiple of 11

videos.answer: The conjecture is false: every multiple of 11, doubled, is still a multiple of 11

source: Figure it Out (number play, question 12)

items.question: Determine whether the statements below are always true, sometimes true, or never true, and explain. (i) The product of a multiple of 6 and a multiple of 3 is a multiple of 9. (ii) The sum of three consecutive even numbers will be divisible by 6. (iii) If abcdef is a multiple of 6, then badcef will be a multiple of 6. (iv) 8(7b − 3) − 4(11b + 1) is a multiple of 12.
steps: (i) 6a × 3b is 18ab, which is 9 × 2ab: always true.
(ii) 2n + (2n + 2) + (2n + 4) is 6n + 6, which is 6(n + 1): always true.
(iii) badcef has the same digits, so the same digit sum (the test for 3), and the same units digit f (the test for 2): always true.
It always leaves a remainder of 8 on division by 12, so (iv) is never true.
items.answer: (i) always (ii) always (iii) always (iv) never

videos.answer: (i) always (ii) always (iii) always (iv) never

items.question: Is the product of two consecutive integers always a multiple of 2? Why? Is the product of three consecutive integers always a multiple of 6? Why or why not? What can you say about the product of 4 consecutive integers? What about the product of five consecutive integers?
steps: Of two consecutive integers one is even, so their product is a multiple of 2.
Of three consecutive integers one is a multiple of 3 and at least one is even, so the product is a multiple of 6: 4 × 5 × 6 = 120.
Four consecutive integers hold a multiple of 4, another even number and a multiple of 3, so the product is a multiple of 24: 1 × 2 × 3 × 4 = 24.
Five consecutive integers also hold a multiple of 5, so the product is a multiple of 120: 1 × 2 × 3 × 4 × 5 = 120.
items.answer: Always a multiple of 2, of 6, of 24 and of 120 respectively

videos.answer: Always a multiple of 2, of 6, of 24 and of 120 respectively

source: Figure it Out (number play, question 16)

items.question: Which of the four Venn diagrams captures the relationship between the multiples of 4, 8, and 32?
steps: Every multiple of 32 is 8 × 4k, so it is also a multiple of 8.
Every multiple of 8 is 4 × 2k, so it is also a multiple of 4.
But 4 is not a multiple of 8, and 8 is not a multiple of 32.
So the circle for multiples of 32 sits inside the circle for multiples of 8, which sits inside the circle for multiples of 4.
items.answer: Diagram (iv): multiples of 32 inside multiples of 8, inside multiples of 4

videos.answer: Diagram (iv): multiples of 32 inside multiples of 8, inside multiples of 4

source: Which of 3k + 5, 3k − 5, 3k ÷ 5, 5k + 3, 5k − 2 and 5k − 3 g

items.question: Which of 3k + 5, 3k − 5, 3k ÷ 5, 5k + 3, 5k − 2 and 5k − 3 give exactly the numbers that leave remainder 3 on division by 5?
steps: The numbers are 3, 8, 13, 18, 23 and so on, each 5 more than the one before.
5k + 3 with k = 0, 1, 2, 3 gives 3, 8, 13, 18, and 5k − 2 with k = 1, 2, 3, 4 gives the same numbers.
3k + 5 with k = 2 gives 11, which leaves remainder 1; 3k − 5 with k = 2 gives 1.
5k − 3 with k = 1 gives 2, and 3k ÷ 5 is often not even a whole number.
items.answer: 5k + 3 (k from 0) and 5k − 2 (k from 1); the other four do not work

videos.answer: 5k + 3 (k from 0) and 5k − 2 (k from 1); the other four do not work

source: 17 leaves remainder 2 and 24 leaves remainder 4 on division

items.question: 17 leaves remainder 2 and 24 leaves remainder 4 on division by 5. Without adding, find the remainders of 17 + 24 and 24 − 17 on division by 5.
steps: Sum: the multiples make 5 × 7 and the remainders make 6, which is 5 + 1, so the remainder is 1.
Difference: the multiples make 5 × 1 and the remainders make 4 − 2, so the remainder is 2.
items.answer: 17 + 24 leaves remainder 1 and 24 − 17 leaves remainder 2

videos.answer: 17 + 24 leaves remainder 1 and 24 − 17 leaves remainder 2

source: Find numbers that leave remainder 1 on division by 2 and rem

items.question: Find numbers that leave remainder 1 on division by 2 and remainder 1 on division by 3, and write one expression for all of them.
steps: Odd numbers leave remainder 1 on division by 2: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13.
Of these, 1, 7 and 13 leave remainder 1 on division by 3.
One less than each, 0, 6 and 12, is a multiple of both 2 and 3, so a multiple of 6.
So the numbers are 6k + 1, and they repeat every 6.
items.answer: 1, 7, 13, 19, and so on: all numbers of the form 6k + 1

videos.answer: 1, 7, 13, 19, and so on: all numbers of the form 6k + 1

items.question: Find a few numbers that leave a remainder of 2 when divided by 3 and a remainder of 2 when divided by 4. Write an algebraic expression to describe all such numbers.
steps: Take 2 away: the number becomes a multiple of 3 and of 4, so a multiple of 12.
So the numbers are 12k + 2: 2, 14, 26, 38 and so on.
items.answer: 2, 14, 26, 38, ...; all numbers of the form 12k + 2

videos.answer: 2, 14, 26, 38, ...; all numbers of the form 12k + 2

items.question: "I hold some pebbles, not too many. When I group them in 3's, one stays with me. Try pairing them up, it simply won't do, a stubborn odd pebble remains in my view. Group them by 5, yet one's still around, but grouping by seven, perfection is found. More than one hundred would be far too bold. Can you tell me the number of pebbles I hold?"
steps: One pebble is left over when grouping by 3, by 2 and by 5.
So one less than the number is a multiple of 30: the number is 31, 61 or 91 below one hundred.
Grouping by 7 leaves nothing: 31 and 61 are not multiples of 7, but 91 = 7 × 13.
items.answer: 91 pebbles

videos.answer: 91 pebbles

items.question: Tathagat has written several numbers that leave a remainder of 2 when divided by 6. He claims, "If you add any three such numbers, the sum will always be a multiple of 6." Is Tathagat's claim true?
steps: Write the three numbers as 6a + 2, 6b + 2 and 6c + 2.
Their sum is 6a + 6b + 6c + 6, which is 6(a + b + c + 1).
Check: 2 + 8 + 14 = 24, a multiple of 6.
items.answer: Yes, the claim is true: the three remainders of 2 make 6

videos.answer: Yes, the claim is true: the three remainders of 2 make 6

items.question: When divided by 7, the number 661 leaves a remainder of 3, and 4779 leaves a remainder of 5. Without calculating, can you say what remainders the following expressions will leave when divided by 7? Show the solution both algebraically and visually. (i) 4779 + 661 (ii) 4779 − 661
steps: Write 661 as 7m + 3 and 4779 as 7n + 5.
(i) The sum is 7(m + n) + 8; the 8 left over makes one more group of 7 with 1 left, so the remainder is 1.
(ii) The difference is 7(n − m) + 2, so the remainder is 2.
Visually: rows of 7 dots with 5 and 3 dots left over; the leftovers join to make a full row and 1 more, or 5 minus 3 leaves 2.
items.answer: (i) remainder 1 (ii) remainder 2

videos.answer: (i) remainder 1 (ii) remainder 2

items.question: Find a number that leaves a remainder of 2 when divided by 3, a remainder of 3 when divided by 4, and a remainder of 4 when divided by 5. What is the smallest such number? Can you give a simple explanation of why it is the smallest?
steps: Each remainder is one less than the divisor, so one more than the number is a multiple of 3, 4 and 5.
The smallest common multiple of 3, 4 and 5 is their LCM, 60, so the number is 59.
items.answer: 59; it is the smallest because 60 is the smallest common multiple of 3, 4 and 5

videos.answer: 59; it is the smallest because 60 is the smallest common multiple of 3, 4 and 5

source: Figure it Out (number play, question 2)

items.question: "I take a number that leaves a remainder of 8 when divided by 12. I take another number which is 4 short of a multiple of 12. Their sum will always be a multiple of 8", claims Snehal. Examine his claim and justify your conclusion.
steps: Write the numbers as 12n + 8 and 12m − 4.
Their sum is 12(n + m) + 4, which is always 4 more than a multiple of 12.
8 and 8 fit and make 16, a multiple of 8; but 20 and 8 fit too and make 28, which is not.
So the sum is always a multiple of 4, but only sometimes a multiple of 8.
items.answer: The claim is false: the sum is 12(n + m) + 4, a multiple of 8 only sometimes (for example 28 is not)

videos.answer: The claim is false: the sum is 12(n + m) + 4, a multiple of 8 only sometimes (for example 28 is not)

items.question: Find three consecutive numbers such that the first number is a multiple of 2, the second number is a multiple of 3, and the third number is a multiple of 4. Are there more such numbers? How often do they occur?
steps: Try small numbers: 2, 3 and 4 work.
If n, n + 1 and n + 2 work, then n − 2 is a multiple of 2, of 3 and of 4, so a multiple of 12.
items.answer: 2, 3, 4 and 14, 15, 16 and so on; a new set occurs every 12 numbers

videos.answer: 2, 3, 4 and 14, 15, 16 and so on; a new set occurs every 12 numbers

source: Figure it Out (number play, question 13)

items.question: Choose any 3 numbers. When is their sum divisible by 3? Explore all possible cases and generalise.
steps: Look at the remainders of the three numbers on division by 3: each is 0, 1 or 2.
The sum is divisible by 3 when the remainders add to 0, 3 or 6.
That happens when all three remainders are the same, as in 4 + 7 + 10 = 21, or all different, as in 3 + 4 + 5 = 12.
In every other case it is not, as in 1 + 2 + 4 = 7.
items.answer: When the three numbers leave the same remainder on division by 3, or three different remainders

videos.answer: When the three numbers leave the same remainder on division by 3, or three different remainders

source: Write 4075 and 4070 as sums of place values and decide which

items.question: Write 4075 and 4070 as sums of place values and decide which is divisible by 10.
steps: 4 × 1000, 0 × 100 and 7 × 10 are multiples of 10; only the units digit 5 is left over.
4070 = 4 × 1000 + 0 × 100 + 7 × 10 + 0, so nothing is left over.
items.answer: 4070 is divisible by 10 and 4075 is not; only the units digit decides

videos.answer: 4070 is divisible by 10 and 4075 is not; only the units digit decides

source: Use place values to decide whether 3716 and 4075 are divisib

items.question: Use place values to decide whether 3716 and 4075 are divisible by 5 and by 2.
steps: 3716 = 3 × 1000 + 7 × 100 + 1 × 10 + 6, and every term except 6 is a multiple of 10.
6 is even but not 0 or 5, so 3716 is divisible by 2 and not by 5.
4075 = 4 × 1000 + 7 × 10 + 5, and only the units digit 5 is left to test.
5 is a multiple of 5 but odd, so 4075 is divisible by 5 and not by 2.
items.answer: 3716 is divisible by 2 only; 4075 is divisible by 5 only

videos.answer: 3716 is divisible by 2 only; 4075 is divisible by 5 only

source: Checking Divisibility Quickly: the shortcuts for 4 and 8

items.question: Explain using algebra why the divisibility shortcuts for 4 and 8 work. Use them to test 3716 for 4 and 51240 for 8.
steps: 100 = 4 × 25, so 100c, 1000d and every higher place value are multiples of 4.
So a number is divisible by 4 exactly when its last two digits, 10b + a, form a multiple of 4.
1000 = 8 × 125, so 1000d and every higher place value are multiples of 8, and the last three digits decide divisibility by 8.
3716 ends in 16, which is 4 × 4, so 3716 is divisible by 4.
51240 ends in 240, which is 8 × 30, so 51240 is divisible by 8.
items.answer: 4 needs the last two digits and 8 the last three; 3716 is divisible by 4 and 51240 by 8

videos.answer: 4 needs the last two digits and 8 the last three; 3716 is divisible by 4 and 51240 by 8

source: Explain why 99009 is divisible by 9, and why 109 is not even

items.question: Explain why 99009 is divisible by 9, and why 109 is not even though it ends in 9.
steps: Every term is 9 times a place value or zero, so the sum is a multiple of 9.
109 = 99 + 10, and 10 = 9 + 1, so 109 is 1 more than a multiple of 9.
items.answer: 99009 is a multiple of 9; 109 leaves remainder 1, so a units digit of 9 proves nothing

videos.answer: 99009 is a multiple of 9; 109 leaves remainder 1, so a units digit of 9 proves nothing

source: Find the remainders of 427 and 7309 on division by 9 without

items.question: Find the remainders of 427 and 7309 on division by 9 without dividing.
steps: 427 = 4 × 99 + 2 × 9 + 4 + 2 + 7, so the leftovers are 4, 2 and 7.
4 + 2 + 7 = 13, and 13 = 9 + 4, so 427 leaves remainder 4.
7309 = 7 × 999 + 3 × 99 + 7 + 3 + 0 + 9, so the leftovers add to 19.
19 = 9 + 10 and 10 = 9 + 1, so 7309 leaves remainder 1.
items.answer: 427 leaves remainder 4 and 7309 leaves remainder 1

steps: (i) 3 × T ends in T, so T is 0 or 5; T = 5 fails because 3 × U + 1 cannot end in U, and T = 0 gives 50 × 3 = 150.

(v) PP × QQ is P × Q × 121, and a 3-digit product needs P × Q to be at most 8.
The units digit of the product is then P × Q itself, and it must be P, so Q = 1: 22 × 11 = 242, 33 × 11 = 363, 44 × 11 = 484.
